pyq_focus: Unit 4 se har paper mein 8-10 sawal aate hain, aur unseen prose passage bhi isi unit ka hissa maana jaata hai.
Sabse zyada pooche gaye naam: Bacon aur Samuel Johnson; uske baad Lamb, Hazlitt, Carlyle, Swift, Addison-Steele aur De Quincey.
17th century prose (Burton, Browne, Hobbes, Locke, Milton ke tracts, Pepys) pichhle kuch saalon mein bahut aaya hai - ise halke mein mat lo.
Sawal ka pattern: 'yeh quote kis essay ka hai', 'yeh essay kis collection mein hai', persona/pseudonym (Bickerstaff, Elia, Democritus Junior), aur saal.
Match-the-following mein author-work, periodical-editor aur persona-periodical pairs aate hain; chronology mein ek author ke 4 works ka order.
Victorian sages (Carlyle, Ruskin, Arnold, Newman, Mill, Pater) ke key terms yaad karo: cash nexus, pathetic fallacy, sweetness and light, gem-like flame.
Modern mein Woolf (Room of One's Own) aur Orwell (Politics and the English Language, Shooting an Elephant) almost har saal; Russell aur Strachey kabhi-kabhi.
Indian non-fiction: Gandhi, Nehru, Ambedkar, Tagore, Nirad Chaudhuri, Dalit autobiographies - title + saal + language yaad rakho.
Tayari ka tarika: har author ke 3-4 works saal ke saath ek line mein likho, 1-2 famous quotes ratto, aur roz 10 MCQ lagao.
American aur postcolonial prose (Emerson, Thoreau, Du Bois, Baldwin, Achebe, Atwood ki Survival) se bhi ek-do sawal aa jaate hain.

easy.title: The Essay: Origins and Francis Bacon
easy.story: Essay ka matlab hai 'koshish' - French shabd 'essai' se aaya. Montaigne ne 1580 mein apne mann ki baatein likhi, jaise koi diary mein dil khol de. Phir Francis Bacon aaya, jo dadaji ki tarah chhote-chhote gyaan bhare vaakya bolta tha. Jaise dadaji kehte hain 'padhai se aadmi pura banta hai', waise hi Bacon ne 'Of Studies' mein likha. Uske Essays teen baar chhape: 1597 mein 10, 1612 mein 38 aur 1625 mein 58. Isiliye Bacon ko English essay ka pita kehte hain.
easy.trick: 10-38-58 = 'Das ka note, Adtees ki chai, Atthawan ki thali' - 1597, 1612, 1625. Idols ke liye 'TCMT': Tribe, Cave, Market, Theatre = 'Tau Chacha Mandi Theatre'.

easy.title: Seventeenth-Century Prose: Browne, Burton, Walton and Others
easy.story: 17vi sadi ke likhne wale bade bhaari, sajaavati vaakya likhte the, jaise shaadi ka card jismein bahut gold design ho. Thomas Browne ek doctor tha jisne 'Religio Medici' mein doctor ka dharm likha. Robert Burton ne udaasi (melancholy) par poori kitaab likh di aur apna naam rakha Democritus Junior. Izaak Walton ne machhli pakadne par baat-cheet wali kitaab likhi, The Compleat Angler. Hobbes ne kaha bina sarkar ke zindagi 'nasty, brutish and short' hoti hai.
easy.trick: Browne = 'Bhai doctor' (Religio Medici), Burton = 'Bura mood' (Melancholy 1621), Walton = 'Waah machhli' (Angler 1653), Hobbes = 'Hukoomat chahiye' (Leviathan 1651).

easy.title: Milton's Prose
easy.story: Milton sirf kavi nahi tha, usne bahut saare pamphlet bhi likhe. Usne apne gadya ko 'left hand' ka kaam kaha, matlab ulte haath ka kaam. 1643 mein sarkar ne niyam banaya ki koi bhi kitaab chhapne se pehle permission lo. Milton ko yeh bilkul pasand nahi aaya, jaise koi kahe ki WhatsApp message bhejne se pehle teacher se sign karwao. Isliye 1644 mein usne Areopagitica likha aur kaha ki achhi kitaab ko maarna 'reason' ko maarna hai.
easy.trick: 'Areopagitica 1644 = 44 ka license nahi chahiye'. Divorce tracts 1643-45: 'Milton ki shaadi bigdi to talaak par likha'.

easy.title: The Periodical Essay: Addison and Steele
easy.story: Socho 1709-1712 ke London mein log coffee-house mein baith kar roz ek chhota akhbaar padhte the. Steele ne The Tatler shuru kiya aur naam rakha Isaac Bickerstaff. Phir Addison ke saath milkar The Spectator nikala, jismein ek chup-chaap Mr. Spectator sab dekhta hai. Uske club mein gaon ke zamindar Sir Roger de Coverley aur vyapari Sir Andrew Freeport jaise log the. Addison ka maqsad tha ki philosophy library se nikal kar chai ki mez tak pahunche.
easy.trick: 'Tatler = Teen (1709) Steele ka; Spectator = Spec lagake 1711 mein dono dekhte'. Sir Roger = gaon ka Tau (Tory), Freeport = Free trade wala seth (Whig).

easy.title: Samuel Johnson and Boswell
easy.story: Samuel Johnson ek bada vidwaan tha jisne akele 1755 mein English ki Dictionary bana di. Usne The Rambler aur The Idler jaise periodical bhi likhe. Usne Shakespeare ko 'poet of nature' kaha aur 52 kaviyon ki jeevaniyan likhi, Lives of the Poets. Uska ek dost tha James Boswell, jo saaye ki tarah peechhe chalta aur Johnson ki har baat diary mein likh leta. Usi se bani 1791 ki Life of Johnson, jise sabse mahaan English biography maana jaata hai.
easy.trick: '55 mein Dictionary, 65 mein Shakespeare, 75 mein Scotland, 79-81 mein Poets' - Johnson ka har 10 saal ka plan. Boswell = 'Bos ka Well-wisher', 1791.

easy.title: Charles Lamb (Elia)
easy.story: Charles Lamb ek clerk tha jo office ke baad 'Elia' naam se pyaare, mazedaar essays likhta tha. Jaise koi chacha baithkar purani yaadein sunaye, waise hi Lamb apne bachpan aur parivaar ki baatein karta hai. 'Dream-Children' mein woh apne sapnon ke bachchon Alice aur John se baat karta hai, jo asal mein hain hi nahi. 'Roast Pig' mein China ka ek ladka Bo-bo galti se ghar jalaakar bhuna suar ka swaad dhoondh leta hai. Uski behen Mary essays mein 'Bridget Elia' bani hai.
easy.trick: 'Elia ke do dabbe: 1823 pehla, 1833 aakhri (Last Essays)'. Roast Pig = 'Ho-ti Bo-bo, ghar jala, khaana bana'.

easy.title: Romantic Essayists: Hazlitt, Leigh Hunt and De Quincey
easy.story: Romantic daur mein teen gadya-lekhak chamke. Hazlitt ko akele ghoomna pasand tha - 'On Going a Journey' mein kehta hai main akela safar karna chahta hoon. Usne 'The Spirit of the Age' mein apne zamane ke bade logon ki tasveerein banayi. De Quincey ne afeem khane ki aadat par 'Confessions of an English Opium-Eater' likhi, sapnon jaisi bhasha mein. Leigh Hunt ne The Examiner akhbaar chalaya aur Prince Regent ki burai par jail gaya.
easy.trick: Hazlitt = 'Hazrat akele Journey par', De Quincey = 'De Quincey ko de afeem' (1821-22), 'Knocking' = Macbeth ke darwaze pe thak-thak.

easy.title: Thomas Carlyle
easy.story: Carlyle Scotland ka ek gussail sant jaisa lekhak tha, jise 'Sage of Chelsea' kehte hain. Usne kaha tumhara zamana machine ka zamana ban gaya hai. 'Sartor Resartus' mein ek ajeeb German professor Teufelsdrockh kapdon ki philosophy samjhaata hai - jaise kehna ki samaj ke rules bhi kapdon ki tarah badalte hain. Usne 'On Heroes' mein kaha duniya ka itihaas bade logon ki jeevani hai. Uski French Revolution ki pehli copy Mill ki naukrani ne galti se jala di thi.
easy.trick: Sartor ke teen padaav: 'Na - Beech - Haan' = Everlasting No, Centre of Indifference, Everlasting Yea. Heroes ke 6 roop: 'DPPPMK' = Divinity, Prophet, Poet, Priest, Man of Letters, King.

easy.title: John Ruskin
easy.story: Ruskin pehle kala ka critic tha - usne painter Turner ka bachav karne ke liye Modern Painters likha. Usne 'pathetic fallacy' shabd banaya: jab kavi kehta hai 'aasmaan ro raha hai', to woh apni bhavna prakriti par daal raha hai. Phir woh arthshastra ki taraf mudda aur 'Unto This Last' mein bola 'There is no wealth but life'. Gandhiji ne yeh kitaab train mein padhi aur Gujarati mein 'Sarvodaya' bana diya. Uski aatmakatha ka naam Praeterita hai.
easy.trick: Ruskin ki ladder: 'Painters (1843) - Lamps (1849) - Stones (1851) - Unto (1860) - Sesame (1865) - Fors (1871) - Praeterita (1885)' = 'Paint, Lamp, Patthar, Paisa, Phool, Chitthi, Purani yaadein'.

easy.title: Matthew Arnold's Prose Criticism
easy.story: Matthew Arnold ek school inspector aur kavi tha jo samaj ka 'culture doctor' banna chahta tha. Usne kaha criticism ka kaam hai duniya ki sabse achhi soch ko seekhna aur failana, bina swarth ke. 'Culture and Anarchy' mein usne samaj ko teen hisson mein baanta: Barbarians (raees), Philistines (madhyam varg) aur Populace (aam janta). Usne 'sweetness and light' Swift se udhaar liya. 'The Study of Poetry' mein usne kavita ko 'criticism of life' kaha.
easy.trick: 'BPP' = 'Bade, Paise-wale, Public' = Barbarians, Philistines, Populace. Hebraism = 'Hukm maano', Hellenism = 'Hosh se socho'.

easy.title: Walter Pater, Aestheticism and Wilde
easy.story: Walter Pater kehta tha zindagi ka har pal poori chamak se jiyo, 'hard, gem-like flame' ki tarah, jaise Diwali ka diya. Uski 'The Renaissance' (1873) ne naujawaanon ko 'art for art's sake' ki taraf khincha. Is soch ko Aestheticism kehte hain - kala ka kaam sirf sundar hona hai, upadesh dena nahi. Oscar Wilde iska sabse chamakdaar chela tha, jisne kaha 'Life imitates Art'. Jail mein Wilde ne lambi chitthi likhi jo De Profundis bani.
easy.trick: Pater = 'Patakha jaisi gem-like flame' (1873). Wilde ulta bolta hai: 'Zindagi kala ki nakal karti hai'.

easy.title: Newman, Mill, Macaulay and Victorian Thought
easy.story: Victorian England mein dharm aur vigyan ki badi behas chal rahi thi. Newman ne Oxford Movement chalaya, phir Catholic ban gaya, aur jab Kingsley ne uski imaandari par sawal uthaya to Apologia Pro Vita Sua likhi. J. S. Mill ne On Liberty mein kaha ek aadmi ki alag raay ko bhi dabana galat hai. Macaulay ne 1835 ki Minute mein India mein English shiksha ki wakalat ki. Huxley aur Arnold mein behas hui ki science badi ya literature.
easy.trick: Newman = 'New Man' bana Catholic 1845. Mill ki 1859 = 'Liberty', 1869 = 'Ladies' (Subjection of Women). Macaulay = 'Minute 1835, ek shelf ki kahani'.

easy.title: Virginia Woolf as Essayist
easy.story: Virginia Woolf ne poocha: ladkiyan bade lekhak kyun nahi bani? Uska jawab tha - paisa aur apna ek kamra chahiye, jahan koi disturb na kare. Isliye 'A Room of One's Own' (1929) likhi, jismein Shakespeare ki kalpanik behen Judith ki dukhbhari kahani hai. Usne kaha 1910 ke aas-paas insaan ka svabhaav badal gaya. Usne Bennett jaise purane novelists ko 'materialists' kaha jo sirf bahari cheezein dikhate hain. 'Professions for Women' mein usne ghar ki 'Angel in the House' ko maar daalne ki baat ki.
easy.trick: 'Room 1929 = Rupaye + Room'. Judith = Shakespeare ki behen. 'December 1910 mein insaan badla' = 1910 = 'Unnees-Dus, sab badal-bas'.

easy.title: Orwell, Russell and Other Modern Essayists
easy.story: George Orwell ka asli naam Eric Blair tha aur woh Bihar ke Motihari mein paida hua tha. Burma mein police officer banke usne angrezi raaj ki sachchai dekhi aur 'Shooting an Elephant' likha. 'Politics and the English Language' mein usne kaha seedhi, saaf bhasha likho, lambe shabd mat bharo. Bertrand Russell ek bada philosopher tha jise 1950 mein Literature ka Nobel mila. Usne kaha uski zindagi teen junoon par chali: pyaar, gyaan aur dukhiyon ke liye dard.
easy.trick: Orwell ke 6 rules ko 'Chhota likho, kaato, active bolo' yaad rakho. Russell ke 3 passions = 'Pyaar, Padhai, Peeda'.

easy.title: Indian Non-Fiction: Gandhi, Nehru and Ambedkar
easy.story: Gandhiji ne 1909 mein jahaz par baithkar 'Hind Swaraj' likhi - ek Reader aur Editor ki baat-cheet, jismein modern civilisation ki aalochana hai. Unki aatmakatha 'Satya ke Prayog' Gujarati mein likhi gayi aur Mahadev Desai ne English mein laaye. Nehru ne jail mein baithkar beti Indira ko chitthiyan likhi aur 'The Discovery of India' likhi. Ambedkar ne 1936 mein 'Annihilation of Caste' likha - ek bhashan jo kabhi diya hi nahi gaya. Unhone kaha jaati ek deewar nahi, mann ki soch hai.
easy.trick: 'Gandhi 09, Nehru 46, Ambedkar 36' = 'Gaadi 9 baje, Netaji 46 mein azaad, Ambedkar 36 mein bhashan'. Hind Swaraj = Kildonan Castle jahaz.

easy.title: Indian Non-Fiction: Tagore, Sen and Other Voices
easy.story: Tagore ne sirf Gitanjali nahi, English mein bhaashan aur nibandh bhi likhe. 'Nationalism' (1917) mein unhone kaha Western nation-state ek machine ki tarah insaaniyat ko kuchal deti hai. Amartya Sen ne 'The Argumentative Indian' mein bataya ki Bharat mein behas karne ki purani parampara hai. Nirad C. Chaudhuri ne apni aatmakatha British Empire ki yaad ko samarpit kar di. Dalit lekhakon jaise Bama aur Omprakash Valmiki ne apni peeda ki sachchi kahaniyan likhi.
easy.trick: Tagore = '1917 Nationalism, 1941 Crisis'. Sen = 'Sen saab behas karte' (Argumentative 2005). Joothan = Hindi 1997, Karukku = Tamil 1992.

easy.title: Biography, Autobiography and Diary
easy.story: Biography matlab kisi aur ki zindagi likhna, autobiography matlab apni khud ki. Boswell ne Johnson ki zindagi aise likhi jaise koi best friend sab raaz jaanta ho. 1918 mein Lytton Strachey ne 'Eminent Victorians' mein bade logon ka mazaak udaya, ise 'new biography' kaha gaya. Diary mein log roz ki baatein likhte hain - Samuel Pepys ne 1660-69 ki diary code bhasha mein likhi. Saint ki jeevani ko hagiography kehte hain.
easy.trick: 'Bio = doosre ki, Auto = apni, Diary = roz ki'. Pepys = 'Peeps' karke chupke se shorthand mein likhta tha (1825 mein chhapi).

easy.title: Travel Writing and Periodicals
easy.story: Travel writing yaani safar ki kahani, jaise koi Goa trip se aakar sabko vlog dikhaye. Purani 'Travels of Sir John Mandeville' mein aadhi baatein kalpanik thi. Kinglake ne 'Eothen' mein Turkey-Middle East ki yatra likhi aur Naipaul ne India par 'An Area of Darkness' likhi. Saath hi 19vi sadi mein magazines ka zamana tha: Edinburgh Review, Quarterly Review, Blackwood's. Inhi patrikaon mein Lamb, Hazlitt aur De Quincey chhape aur inhone Keats jaise kaviyon ki burai bhi ki.
easy.trick: Review ka order: 'Edinburgh 1802, Quarterly 1809, Blackwood's 1817, London 1820' = 'E-Q-B-L = Eat Quick Bread Loaf'.

quotes.quote: I am myself the matter of my book.
What is truth? said jesting Pilate, and would not stay for an answer.
Studies serve for delight, for ornament, and for ability.
Reading maketh a full man; conference a ready man; and writing an exact man.
Revenge is a kind of wild justice; which the more man's nature runs to, the more ought law to weed it out.
He that hath wife and children hath given hostages to fortune.
Men fear death, as children fear to go in the dark.
God Almighty first planted a garden.
Man is a noble animal, splendid in ashes, and pompous in the grave.
No man is an island, entire of itself.
quotes.source: Devotions upon Emergent Occasions, Meditation XVII (1624)

quotes.quote: And the life of man, solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short.
A good book is the precious life-blood of a master spirit, embalmed and treasured up on purpose to a life beyond life.
Who kills a man kills a reasonable creature, God's image; but he who destroys a good book, kills reason itself.
Let her and Falsehood grapple; who ever knew Truth put to the worse, in a free and open encounter?
I cannot praise a fugitive and cloistered virtue, unexercised and unbreathed.
Instead of dirt and poison we have rather chosen to fill our hives with honey and wax; thus furnishing mankind with the two noblest of things, which are sweetness and light.
I shall be ambitious to have it said of me, that I have brought philosophy out of closets and libraries, schools and colleges, to dwell in clubs and assemblies, at tea-tables and in coffee-houses.
Is not a patron, my Lord, one who looks with unconcern on a man struggling for life in the water, and, when he has reached ground, encumbers him with help?
Lexicographer: a writer of dictionaries; a harmless drudge.
quotes.source: A Dictionary of the English Language (1755)

quotes.quote: Shakespeare is above all writers, at least above all modern writers, the poet of nature; the poet that holds up to his readers a faithful mirrour of manners and of life.
The most heterogeneous ideas are yoked by violence together.
quotes.source: Life of Cowley, Lives of the Poets (1779)

quotes.quote: When a man is tired of London, he is tired of life; for there is in London all that life can afford.
quotes.source: Boswell, The Life of Samuel Johnson (1791)

quotes.quote: They order, said I, this matter better in France.
But the age of chivalry is gone. That of sophisters, economists, and calculators, has succeeded.
quotes.source: Reflections on the Revolution in France (1790)

quotes.quote: We are not of Alice, nor of thee, nor are we children at all.
One of the pleasantest things in the world is going a journey; but I like to go by myself.
There is, first, the literature of knowledge; and secondly, the literature of power. The function of the first is to teach; the function of the second is to move.
Close thy Byron; open thy Goethe.
The history of the world is but the biography of great men.
quotes.source: On Heroes, Hero-Worship and the Heroic in History (1841)

quotes.quote: There is no wealth but life.
A disinterested endeavour to learn and propagate the best that is known and thought in the world.
quotes.source: 'The Function of Criticism at the Present Time' (1864)

quotes.quote: Poetry is at bottom a criticism of life.
A beautiful and ineffectual angel, beating in the void his luminous wings in vain.
To burn always with this hard, gem-like flame, to maintain this ecstasy, is success in life.
All art constantly aspires towards the condition of music.
Life imitates Art far more than Art imitates Life.
It is almost a definition of a gentleman to say he is one who never inflicts pain.
Eloquence is heard; poetry is overheard.

If all mankind minus one were of one opinion, and only one person were of the contrary opinion, mankind would be no more justified in silencing that one person, than he, if he had the power, would be justified in silencing mankind.
A single shelf of a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia.
Ignorance is the first requisite of the historian.
A woman must have money and a room of her own if she is to write fiction.
On or about December 1910 human character changed.
Life is not a series of gig lamps symmetrically arranged; life is a luminous halo.
Good prose is like a window pane.
Political language is designed to make lies sound truthful and murder respectable, and to give an appearance of solidity to pure wind.
Three passions, simple but overwhelmingly strong, have governed my life: the longing for love, the search for knowledge, and unbearable pity for the suffering of mankind.
Long years ago we made a tryst with destiny, and now the time comes when we shall redeem our pledge.
A foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds.
The mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation.

mcqs.exp: Wordsworth ki kavita se Mill theek hua.

mcqs.q: Pater's Marius the Epicurean is set in:
options: Rome in the age of Marcus Aurelius
mcqs.exp: Marcus Aurelius ka Rome.

mcqs.q: Which work contains the line 'Ignorance is the first requisite of the historian'?
mcqs.exp: Strachey ki Eminent Victorians ki preface.

mcqs.q: Woolf borrowed the phrase 'the Angel in the House' from:
mcqs.exp: Patmore ki kavita 'The Angel in the House'.

mcqs.q: Orwell's 'Such, Such Were the Joys' recalls his days at:
mcqs.exp: St Cyprian's prep school ki yaadein.

mcqs.q: 'A Free Man's Worship' by Russell is collected in:
mcqs.exp: Mysticism and Logic (1918).

mcqs.q: C. P. Snow's 'The Two Cultures' (1959) was famously attacked by:
mcqs.exp: Leavis ka Richmond Lecture 1962.

mcqs.q: Who called Emerson's 'The American Scholar' America's 'intellectual Declaration of Independence'?
mcqs.exp: Holmes ne kaha tha.

mcqs.q: Match the periodical with its founder/editor. List I: (a) The Tatler; (b) The Rambler; (c) The Examiner (1808); (d) The Criterion || List II: (i) Samuel Johnson; (ii) Leigh Hunt; (iii) T. S. Eliot; (iv) Richard Steele
mcqs.exp: Tatler-Steele, Rambler-Johnson, Examiner-Hunt, Criterion-Eliot.

mcqs.q: Match the work with its author. List I: (a) The Anatomy of Melancholy; (b) The Compleat Angler; (c) Leviathan; (d) Holy Dying || List II: (i) Thomas Hobbes; (ii) Jeremy Taylor; (iii) Robert Burton; (iv) Izaak Walton
mcqs.exp: Burton, Walton, Hobbes, Taylor.

mcqs.q: Match the essay with the essayist. List I: (a) On Gusto; (b) The Superannuated Man; (c) On Murder Considered as One of the Fine Arts; (d) An Apology for Idlers || List II: (i) Charles Lamb; (ii) R. L. Stevenson; (iii) William Hazlitt; (iv) Thomas De Quincey
mcqs.exp: Gusto-Hazlitt, Superannuated-Lamb, Murder-De Quincey, Idlers-Stevenson.

mcqs.q: Match Arnold's terms in Culture and Anarchy with their meanings. List I: (a) Barbarians; (b) Philistines; (c) Populace; (d) Hellenism || List II: (i) the middle class; (ii) spontaneity of consciousness; (iii) the aristocracy; (iv) the working class
mcqs.exp: Barbarians aristocracy, Philistines middle class, Populace working class, Hellenism spontaneity.

mcqs.q: Match the autobiography with its author. List I: (a) Apologia Pro Vita Sua; (b) Praeterita; (c) Father and Son; (d) Autobiography (1873) || List II: (i) Edmund Gosse; (ii) J. S. Mill; (iii) J. H. Newman; (iv) John Ruskin
mcqs.exp: Newman, Ruskin, Gosse, Mill.

mcqs.q: Match the work with the Indian writer. List I: (a) Gulamgiri; (b) Poverty and Un-British Rule in India; (c) Gita Rahasya; (d) The High-Caste Hindu Woman || List II: (i) Bal Gangadhar Tilak; (ii) Pandita Ramabai; (iii) Jotirao Phule; (iv) Dadabhai Naoroji
mcqs.exp: Phule, Naoroji, Tilak, Ramabai.

mcqs.q: Match the Dalit autobiography with its author. List I: (a) Joothan; (b) Karukku; (c) Akkarmashi; (d) Baluta || List II: (i) Daya Pawar; (ii) Bama; (iii) Omprakash Valmiki; (iv) Sharankumar Limbale
mcqs.exp: Joothan-Valmiki, Karukku-Bama, Akkarmashi-Limbale, Baluta-Pawar.

mcqs.q: Match the travel book with the region it describes. List I: (a) Eothen; (b) Travels in Arabia Deserta; (c) Journey Without Maps; (d) In Patagonia || List II: (i) Liberia; (ii) South America; (iii) the Ottoman Near East; (iv) Arabia
mcqs.exp: Kinglake-Near East, Doughty-Arabia, Greene-Liberia, Chatwin-Patagonia.

mcqs.q: Match the American work with its author. List I: (a) Walden; (b) The Souls of Black Folk; (c) Letters from an American Farmer; (d) Self-Reliance || List II: (i) R. W. Emerson; (ii) H. D. Thoreau; (iii) W. E. B. Du Bois; (iv) J. Hector St. John de Crevecoeur
mcqs.exp: Thoreau, Du Bois, Crevecoeur, Emerson.

mcqs.q: Match the quotation with its author. List I: (a) 'Good prose is like a window pane.'; (b) 'There is no wealth but life.'; (c) 'Life imitates Art far more than Art imitates Life.'; (d) 'Eloquence is heard; poetry is overheard.' || List II: (i) Oscar Wilde; (ii) J. S. Mill; (iii) George Orwell; (iv) John Ruskin
mcqs.exp: Orwell, Ruskin, Wilde, Mill.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Bacon's essays are aphoristic and impersonal in manner. Reason (R): Bacon modelled his essays as intimate self-portraits in the manner of Montaigne.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.exp: A sahi; R galat - Bacon Montaigne jaise personal nahi the.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Milton's Areopagitica opposes licensing of books before publication. Reason (R): Milton believed that Truth never loses in a free and open encounter with Falsehood.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.exp: Dono sahi aur R hi A ka kaaran hai.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Lamb's Elia essays are regarded as classic familiar essays. Reason (R): Through the persona of Elia, Lamb shares his personal memories, whims and moods.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.exp: Personal yaadein hi unhe familiar essay banati hain.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Ruskin's Unto This Last attacks the classical political economy of his day. Reason (R): Ruskin became the first Slade Professor of Fine Art at Oxford.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.exp: Dono sahi, par R ka A se koi sambandh nahi.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Johnson's Preface to Shakespeare defends the mingling of tragic and comic scenes. Reason (R): Johnson held that Shakespeare's greatness lay in his strict observance of the unities of time and place.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.exp: A sahi; R galat - Johnson ne unities of time and place ko reject kiya.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): A Room of One's Own grew out of lectures Woolf gave at two Oxford colleges. Reason (R): Woolf argues that a woman must have money and a room of her own if she is to write fiction.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.exp: Lectures Cambridge (Newnham, Girton) mein the, isliye A galat; R sahi.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Gandhi's Hind Swaraj is a critique of modern Western civilisation. Reason (R): Hind Swaraj is cast as a dialogue between a Reader and an Editor.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.exp: Dono sahi, par dialogue form critique ka kaaran nahi.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Orwell's 'Shooting an Elephant' is set in British India's Punjab. Reason (R): Orwell served in the Indian Imperial Police in Burma.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.exp: Essay Burma (Moulmein) mein set hai, A galat; R sahi.

mcqs.q: Arrange in chronological order: (i) Areopagitica (ii) Leviathan (iii) Religio Medici (authorised edition) (iv) The Anatomy of Melancholy
mcqs.exp: Anatomy 1621, Religio 1643, Areopagitica 1644, Leviathan 1651.

mcqs.q: Arrange in chronological order: (i) The Spectator (ii) The Rambler (iii) The Tatler (iv) The Idler
mcqs.exp: Tatler 1709, Spectator 1711, Rambler 1750, Idler 1758.

mcqs.q: Arrange in chronological order: (i) Essays of Elia (ii) Confessions of an English Opium-Eater (book) (iii) The Spirit of the Age (iv) The Round Table
mcqs.exp: Round Table 1817, Confessions 1822, Elia 1823, Spirit 1825.

mcqs.q: Arrange in chronological order: (i) Past and Present (ii) Signs of the Times (iii) Latter-Day Pamphlets (iv) The French Revolution
Arrange in chronological order: (i) Culture and Anarchy (ii) On Translating Homer (iii) The Study of Poetry (iv) The Function of Criticism at the Present Time
Arrange in chronological order: (i) Three Guineas (ii) A Room of One's Own (iii) Mr. Bennett and Mrs. Brown (iv) The Common Reader
Arrange in chronological order: (i) The Discovery of India (ii) Hind Swaraj (iii) Annihilation of Caste (iv) The Autobiography of an Unknown Indian
Identify the correct statement.
options: Florio translated Bacon's Essays into French.
Montaigne's Essais were first published in 1580.
Bacon's 1597 edition of the Essays contained 58 essays.
Bacon's New Atlantis was published in his lifetime in 1605.
mcqs.exp: Montaigne 1580 sahi; Bacon 1597 mein 10 essays, New Atlantis 1627 posthumous.

mcqs.q: Identify the correct statement about The Spectator.
options: Sir Roger de Coverley was first introduced by Steele in Spectator No. 2.
The Whig merchant of the Spectator Club is Will Honeycomb.
The Spectator was a monthly magazine.
mcqs.exp: Sir Roger Steele ne No. 2 mein banaya; Tatler Steele ka, Freeport Whig merchant, Spectator daily tha.

mcqs.q: Identify the correct statement about Samuel Johnson.
options: Boswell's Life of Johnson was published in 1785.
A Dictionary of the English Language appeared in 1765.
Rasselas was written to pay for his father's funeral.
Lives of the Poets contains fifty-two lives.
mcqs.exp: 52 lives sahi; Rasselas maa ke funeral ke liye, Dictionary 1755, Life 1791.

mcqs.q: Identify the correct statement about Victorian prose.
options: Mill's The Subjection of Women was published in 1869.
Ruskin's Modern Painters began as a defence of Constable.
Pater's Studies in the History of the Renaissance appeared in 1893.
In Culture and Anarchy Arnold calls the aristocracy Philistines.
mcqs.exp: Subjection 1869 sahi; Modern Painters Turner ke liye, Renaissance 1873, aristocracy = Barbarians.

mcqs.q: Identify the correct statement about George Orwell.
options: 'Politics and the English Language' lays down four rules.
Down and Out is set in Paris and Berlin.
Homage to Catalonia describes the Second World War.
He was born at Motihari in Bihar.
mcqs.exp: Motihari sahi; Catalonia Spanish Civil War, 6 rules, Paris aur London.
